learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to interact positively with the world! Explore the importance of healthy relationships, empathy, and overcoming social evils like substance abuse.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It is your ability to form meaningful relationships, adapt to social situations, interact comfortably with others, and act responsibly in society.
Good social health requires active listening, clear communication, and empathy (putting yourself in someone else's shoes). It helps resolve conflicts peacefully.
The influence from members of your peer group can be positive (encouraging you to study) or negative (pressuring you to break rules). Learning to say 'NO' respectfully is a vital skill.
Using harmful substances like tobacco, alcohol, or drugs destroys physical health, ruins social relationships, and leads to addiction. It often starts due to negative peer pressure or stress.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🕊️ Role of Sports in Social Health
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Team sports teach cooperation, respect for opponents and referees, leadership, and how to handle both victory and defeat gracefully.

fun_activity.title: 📱 Digital Detox Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: Put your phone and all screens away for exactly 2 hours. Use this time to have a real, face-to-face conversation with a family member or play a board game. Real-world connections boost social health!

exam_tips: 📌 Be able to define Social Health clearly (it's the 'social' part of the WHO's definition of health).
📌 Prepare points on how to resist negative peer pressure (assertiveness, avoiding bad company).
📌 Discuss the negative impacts of substance abuse not just on the individual's body, but on their family and society.
quick_recap: ⭐ A socially healthy person treats others with respect and does not discriminate.
⭐ Addiction rewires the brain, making it a severe medical and social issue, not just a 'bad habit'.
⭐ Participating in community service or group sports is the best way to develop social health.
